questions.q: In the Bayer's process, the leaching of alumina is done by using
questions.solution:
In the Bayer's process, the leaching of alumina is done by using $\mathrm{NaOH}$.
$\mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}(s)+2 \mathrm{NaOH}(a q) \stackrel{150^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, 35 \mathrm{atm}}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}\right]+3 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}2 \mathrm{Na}\left[\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}\right]+\mathrm{CO}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3} \cdot x \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}+2 \mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}\mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3} \cdot x \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(s) \underset{\longrightarrow}{\text{1470K}} \mathrm{Al}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{3}(s)+x \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(g)$
So, the option (b) is correct answer.

questions.q: Roasted copper pyrite on smelting with sand produces
options: $\mathrm{FeSiO}_{3}$ as fusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{S}$ as matte
$\mathrm{CaSiO}_{3}$ as infusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{O}$ as matte
$\mathrm{Ca}_{3}\left(\mathrm{PO}_{4}\right)_{2}$ as fusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{S}$ as matte
$\mathrm{Fe}_{3}\left(\mathrm{PO}_{4}\right)_{2}$ as infusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{S}$ as matte
questions.solution:
Roasted copper pyrite on smelting with sand produces $\mathrm{FeSiO}_{3}$ as fusible slag and $\mathrm{Cu}_{2}$ S as matte
For removing the gangue, FeS, silica present in the lining of the Bessemer converter, acts as a flux and forms slag (iron silicate) on reaction with FeO.
$\mathrm{FeS}+3 \mathrm{O}_{2} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{FeO}+2 \mathrm{SO}_{2}\mathrm{FeO}+\mathrm{SiO}_{2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{FeSiO}_{3}$
Copper matte mainly contains $\mathrm{Cu}_{2} \mathrm{S}$ and FeS.

questions.q: The important advantage(s) of Lintz and Donawitz (L.D.) process for the manufacture of steel is (are)
questions.solution:
Lintz and Donawitz (L.D.) process is an important process for manufacturing of steel. In India, Rourkela steel plant is based upon this process.
This process is carried out in a converter similar to bessemer converter having lining (usually refractory made of $\mathrm{Mg} \mathrm{O}$ and $(\mathrm{CaO})$.
In this method scrap iron can be used along with flux in converter : On passing oxygen gas at $4-12$ atm pressure into converter, temperature of $2000-2500^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ range produced which separates C. Si, Mn etc., impurities as slag from
iron quickly remaining pure iron is mixed with spiegeleisen (alloy Fe, $\mathrm{Mn}$, C) to produce better quality steel.

In aluminium extraction by the Bayer process, alumina is extracted from bauxite by sodium hydroxide at high temperature and pressures :
$\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3(\mathrm{~s})+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(1)$

Solid impurities such as $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ and $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ are removed and then $\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH})_4^{-}$is reprecipitated : $2 \mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{OH})_4^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3 \cdot 3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{s})+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-}$(aq) . In the industrial world :
options: Carbon dioxide is added to precipitate the alumina
Temperature and pressure are dropped and the supersaturated solution seeded
